title: Can Anyone Salary Sacrifice? Hourly to Annual Pay Guide with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary with casual loading and super. Can anyone salary sacrifice? Find out in this guide using Fair Work and ATO figures.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours and then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super. The calculator on this site does this for you.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 for casuals. Super is still calculated on the total ordinary earnings including loading.

Salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you give up part of your salary for benefits like a car or extra super. Not all employers offer it, and eligibility depends on your award or agreement. The calculator here does not include salary sacrifice; consult a tax professional for your situation.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

To work out your annual salary from an hourly rate, multiply the rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This site assumes a standard 38-hour week unless you adjust it. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 gross per year.

If you are paid fortnightly, that is roughly $2,010.36 before tax (weekly × 2). The formula works for any hourly rate, but remember it assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The Fair Work Commission sets the casual loading. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). This loading is part of your ordinary earnings for superannuation purposes.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on a $52,269.44 annual salary, the super contribution would be $6,272.33 (12% of $52,269.44), added to your pay by your employer. Super is not deducted from your gross pay; it is an extra cost for the employer.

For award-covered employees, the base rate may be higher than the minimum. Check your award using [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

## Can Anyone Salary Sacrifice?

Salary sacrifice is an agreement where you give up part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, additional super contributions, or electronic devices. It can reduce your taxable income, but it also affects your super guarantee base because ordinary time earnings generally include salary sacrifice amounts.

**Can anyone salary sacrifice?** Not automatically. It depends on your employer’s policy and your award or enterprise agreement. Some awards restrict salary sacrifice, and you cannot sacrifice below the National Minimum Wage. The Australian Taxation Office has rules about what counts as a genuine sacrifice. The calculator on this site does not include salary sacrifice; you should speak to a payroll officer or tax professional to see if it suits you.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is taxed using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). The calculator on [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates your net pay after tax and Medicare. It does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/) is the home page. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). If you are casual, tick the checkbox to add 25% loading. The calculator then shows your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

For more details on super and packaging, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging). For average earnings comparisons, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which is an average, not a median for your job.

Remember: this is an estimate. Your actual pay may vary due to overtime, penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always check your pay slip and consult a professional for personal advice.
